title: SQL prototypes: unit economics warehouse views (scratchpad)
body:
Context
- Goal: prototype SQL for the Unit Economics dashboard views.
- Primary metric: blended $/1M output tokens, with drilldowns by model(+version/quant), region, customer tier.
- This doc is intentionally messy; used to iterate on schemas + query patterns and to capture perf notes.

Assumptions / naming (current as of 2025-02-22)
- Warehouse: Snowflake (database ANALYTICS, schemas RAW + MART). If we move to BigQuery later, the grouping patterns are the same.
- Canonical hourly fact tables intended output of ENG-8426 job:
  - MART.UNIT_ECON_HOURLY  (hourly grain, already cost-attributed)
  - MART.UNIT_ECON_HOURLY_CONFIDENCE (hourly completeness / missing-dim signals)
- Raw-ish inputs (not all exist yet; these are conceptual while we converge on final schema):
  - RAW.METERING_REQUEST_TOKENS (request-level or minute-level; includes streaming flag)
  - RAW.RUNTIME_SIGNALS (cache hit rate, batching efficiency; some missing)
  - RAW.GPU_COST_HOURLY (rate card-applied $ per hour by region/provider/capacity_type)
  - RAW.DIM_REGION_MAP (normalization mapping)
  - RAW.DIM_CUSTOMER_TIER (tier derivation snapshot)
  - RAW.DIM_MODEL_CATALOG (model_id => family/version/alias)

Metric definition (working)
- blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens = (allocated_infra_cost_usd / output_tokens) * 1,000,000
- allocated_infra_cost_usd includes:
  - GPU compute (primary)
  - optionally shared overhead (per ADR-034; controlled by allocation_version)
  - idle capacity treatment is allocation_policy-driven (see ADR-034)
- Important: avoid dividing by 0 tokens; return NULL and track coverage.

Key dimensions (canonicalized)
- model_key: canonical string used for grouping in dashboard (e.g., "llama-3.1-70b@2025-01-30"), plus quantization_profile (e.g., "fp16", "int8-kv", "w4a16")
- region_norm: canonical region ("us-east-1", "eu-west-1", "onprem-emea-01" etc.)
- customer_tier: self_serve | dedicated | private | enterprise
- Optional (v1.1 candidates): route_id (guardrailed), org_id (never exposed in UI tables), capacity_type (on_demand vs reserved)

----------------------------------------
Prototype 0: request-level tokens -> hourly rollup (sanity)
----------------------------------------
Notes:
- Used for validating streaming parity and dimension coverage.
- Not intended as final dashboard query (too slow on large windows).

-- request -> hour rollup
SELECT
  DATE_TRUNC('HOUR', request_started_at) AS hour_ts,
  region_norm,
  customer_tier,
  model_key,
  quantization_profile,
  SUM(output_tokens) AS output_tokens,
  SUM(input_tokens) AS input_tokens,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_streaming THEN output_tokens ELSE 0 END) AS output_tokens_streaming,
  COUNT(*) AS request_count
FROM RAW.METERING_REQUEST_TOKENS
WHERE request_started_at >= DATEADD('DAY', -7, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
ORDER BY 1 DESC;

Perf notes
- For 30d+ windows, request-level scan is too expensive; must hit MART.UNIT_ECON_HOURLY or at least a pre-aggregated tokens table.

----------------------------------------
Prototype 1: canonical hourly table (the thing dashboard should query)
----------------------------------------
Proposed table shape (MART.UNIT_ECON_HOURLY)
- hour_ts (TIMESTAMP)
- allocation_version (STRING)  -- pins rate card + allocation policy version
- region_norm (STRING)
- customer_tier (STRING)
- model_key (STRING)
- model_version (STRING)       -- optional convenience; model_key already includes in some formats
- quantization_profile (STRING)
- output_tokens (NUMBER)
- input_tokens (NUMBER)
- request_count (NUMBER)
- allocated_cost_usd (NUMBER)
- gpu_cost_usd (NUMBER)
- overhead_cost_usd (NUMBER)
- idle_cost_usd (NUMBER)
- cache_hit_rate (FLOAT)       -- from runtime signals aggregation (may be NULL)
- batching_efficiency (FLOAT)  -- from runtime signals aggregation (may be NULL)
- prefill_decode_ratio (FLOAT) -- from runtime signals aggregation (may be NULL)

Create view: unit economics hourly as a stable contract
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW MART.V_UNIT_ECON_HOURLY AS
SELECT
  hour_ts,
  allocation_version,
  region_norm,
  customer_tier,
  model_key,
  quantization_profile,
  output_tokens,
  input_tokens,
  request_count,
  allocated_cost_usd,
  gpu_cost_usd,
  overhead_cost_usd,
  idle_cost_usd,
  cache_hit_rate,
  batching_efficiency,
  prefill_decode_ratio
FROM MART.UNIT_ECON_HOURLY;

----------------------------------------
Prototype 2: dashboard timeseries query (group_by dims)
----------------------------------------
Pattern:
- Query should support:
  - time range
  - filters: model_key(s), region_norm(s), customer_tier(s), quantization_profile(s)
  - group_by: [model_key, region_norm, customer_tier] plus time bucket
  - metric: blended $/1M output tokens

-- Timeseries: blended $/1M output tokens by day
-- (Use DAY bucket for UI default; hourly is too noisy unless zoomed)
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('DAY', hour_ts) AS bucket_ts,
    model_key,
    region_norm,
    customer_tier,
    SUM(output_tokens) AS output_tokens,
    SUM(allocated_cost_usd) AS allocated_cost_usd
  FROM MART.V_UNIT_ECON_HOURLY
  WHERE hour_ts >= :start_ts
    AND hour_ts < :end_ts
    AND allocation_version = :allocation_version
    AND (:model_key_is_all OR model_key IN (SELECT VALUE FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(INPUT => :model_keys))))
    AND (:region_is_all OR region_norm IN (SELECT VALUE FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(INPUT => :regions))))
    AND (:tier_is_all OR customer_tier IN (SELECT VALUE FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(INPUT => :tiers))))
    AND (:quant_is_all OR quantization_profile IN (SELECT VALUE FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(INPUT => :quant_profiles))))
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
SELECT
  bucket_ts,
  model_key,
  region_norm,
  customer_tier,
  output_tokens,
  allocated_cost_usd,
  CASE WHEN output_tokens = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE (allocated_cost_usd / output_tokens) * 1000000
  END AS blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens
FROM base
ORDER BY bucket_ts ASC;

Perf notes
- Use allocation_version as mandatory filter for Finance view stability.
- Avoid cross products with FILTER arrays; prefer dynamic SQL in API layer if needed.
- If UI needs “All models” group, do it as an explicit group_by = none (no model_key in GROUP BY), not by passing huge model list.

----------------------------------------
Prototype 3: top-N tables (e.g., worst $/1M tokens)
----------------------------------------
-- Top 20 most expensive model+region combos (by blended cost) over time range
WITH agg AS (
  SELECT
    model_key,
    region_norm,
    customer_tier,
    SUM(output_tokens) AS output_tokens,
    SUM(allocated_cost_usd) AS allocated_cost_usd
  FROM MART.V_UNIT_ECON_HOURLY
  WHERE hour_ts >= :start_ts
    AND hour_ts < :end_ts
    AND allocation_version = :allocation_version
    AND customer_tier IN ('self_serve','dedicated','private','enterprise')
  GROUP BY 1,2,3
), scored AS (
  SELECT
    model_key,
    region_norm,
    customer_tier,
    output_tokens,
    allocated_cost_usd,
    CASE WHEN output_tokens = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE (allocated_cost_usd / output_tokens) * 1000000
    END AS blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens
  FROM agg
)
SELECT *
FROM scored
WHERE output_tokens >= :min_tokens_threshold
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens DESC NULLS LAST) <= 20;

Notes
- Token threshold is essential. Otherwise small-volume cells dominate “worst cost”.
- For Finance, default min_tokens_threshold suggestion: >= 5M tokens over window (tunable).

----------------------------------------
Prototype 4: “compare to previous period” (basic delta)
----------------------------------------
-- Compare current window vs previous window of same length.
-- Used for “regression detection” and for the exec readout.
WITH params AS (
  SELECT
    :start_ts::TIMESTAMP AS start_ts,
    :end_ts::TIMESTAMP AS end_ts,
    DATEDIFF('SECOND', :start_ts::TIMESTAMP, :end_ts::TIMESTAMP) AS window_secs
), cur AS (
  SELECT
    model_key,
    region_norm,
    customer_tier,
    SUM(output_tokens) AS output_tokens,
    SUM(allocated_cost_usd) AS allocated_cost_usd
  FROM MART.V_UNIT_ECON_HOURLY, params
  WHERE hour_ts >= params.start_ts
    AND hour_ts < params.end_ts
    AND allocation_version = :allocation_version
  GROUP BY 1,2,3
), prev AS (
  SELECT
    model_key,
    region_norm,
    customer_tier,
    SUM(output_tokens) AS output_tokens,
    SUM(allocated_cost_usd) AS allocated_cost_usd
  FROM MART.V_UNIT_ECON_HOURLY, params
  WHERE hour_ts >= DATEADD('SECOND', -params.window_secs, params.start_ts)
    AND hour_ts < params.start_ts
    AND allocation_version = :allocation_version
  GROUP BY 1,2,3
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(cur.model_key, prev.model_key) AS model_key,
  COALESCE(cur.region_norm, prev.region_norm) AS region_norm,
  COALESCE(cur.customer_tier, prev.customer_tier) AS customer_tier,
  cur.output_tokens AS cur_output_tokens,
  prev.output_tokens AS prev_output_tokens,
  CASE WHEN cur.output_tokens = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (cur.allocated_cost_usd / cur.output_tokens) * 1000000 END AS cur_blended_cost_per_1m,
  CASE WHEN prev.output_tokens = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (prev.allocated_cost_usd / prev.output_tokens) * 1000000 END AS prev_blended_cost_per_1m,
  (cur_blended_cost_per_1m - prev_blended_cost_per_1m) AS delta_blended_cost_per_1m
FROM (
  SELECT *,
    CASE WHEN output_tokens = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (allocated_cost_usd / output_tokens) * 1000000 END AS blended_cost_per_1m
  FROM cur
) cur
FULL OUTER JOIN (
  SELECT *,
    CASE WHEN output_tokens = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (allocated_cost_usd / output_tokens) * 1000000 END AS blended_cost_per_1m
  FROM prev
) prev
ON cur.model_key = prev.model_key
AND cur.region_norm = prev.region_norm
AND cur.customer_tier = prev.customer_tier
ORDER BY delta_blended_cost_per_1m DESC NULLS LAST;

----------------------------------------
Prototype 5: confidence / coverage indicator (missing dims, freshness)
----------------------------------------
Motivation
- Finance signoff blockers include “is this complete?” for a given day.
- Need a way to display warning banner when some % of tokens are missing region/tier/model/quant dims.

Proposed helper view
- Output is one row per bucket_ts (day) per allocation_version.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW MART.V_UNIT_ECON_DAILY_COVERAGE AS
WITH daily AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('DAY', hour_ts) AS day_ts,
    allocation_version,
    SUM(output_tokens) AS output_tokens_total,
    SUM(CASE WHEN region_norm IS NULL OR region_norm IN ('unknown','unmapped') THEN output_tokens ELSE 0 END) AS tokens_missing_region,
    SUM(CASE WHEN customer_tier IS NULL OR customer_tier = 'unknown' THEN output_tokens ELSE 0 END) AS tokens_missing_tier,
    SUM(CASE WHEN model_key IS NULL OR model_key = 'unknown' THEN output_tokens ELSE 0 END) AS tokens_missing_model,
    SUM(CASE WHEN quantization_profile IS NULL OR quantization_profile = 'unknown' THEN output_tokens ELSE 0 END) AS tokens_missing_quant
  FROM MART.V_UNIT_ECON_HOURLY
  WHERE hour_ts >= DATEADD('DAY', -45, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
  GROUP BY 1,2
)
SELECT
  day_ts,
  allocation_version,
  output_tokens_total,
  tokens_missing_region,
  tokens_missing_tier,
  tokens_missing_model,
  tokens_missing_quant,
  CASE WHEN output_tokens_total = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 1.0 - (tokens_missing_region / output_tokens_total) END AS coverage_region,
  CASE WHEN output_tokens_total = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 1.0 - (tokens_missing_tier / output_tokens_total) END AS coverage_tier,
  CASE WHEN output_tokens_total = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 1.0 - (tokens_missing_model / output_tokens_total) END AS coverage_model,
  CASE WHEN output_tokens_total = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 1.0 - (tokens_missing_quant / output_tokens_total) END AS coverage_quant
FROM daily;

Notes
- Dashboard can compute “overall confidence” as min(coverage_region, coverage_tier, coverage_model, coverage_quant) with thresholds:
  - green >= 0.995
  - yellow >= 0.98
  - red < 0.98
- This is approximate; SLO doc will define exact thresholds.

----------------------------------------
Prototype 6: join in runtime signals (cache/batching)
----------------------------------------
If signals are stored separately (hourly), join by hour_ts + dim keys.

WITH econ AS (
  SELECT
    hour_ts,
    allocation_version,
    region_norm,
    customer_tier,
    model_key,
    quantization_profile,
    output_tokens,
    allocated_cost_usd
  FROM MART.UNIT_ECON_HOURLY
  WHERE hour_ts >= :start_ts AND hour_ts < :end_ts
    AND allocation_version = :allocation_version
), sig AS (
  SELECT
    hour_ts,
    region_norm,
    customer_tier,
    model_key,
    quantization_profile,
    AVG(cache_hit_rate) AS cache_hit_rate,
    AVG(batching_efficiency) AS batching_efficiency
  FROM MART.RUNTIME_SIGNALS_HOURLY
  WHERE hour_ts >= :start_ts AND hour_ts < :end_ts
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
)
SELECT
  econ.*, sig.cache_hit_rate, sig.batching_efficiency,
  CASE WHEN econ.output_tokens = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (econ.allocated_cost_usd / econ.output_tokens) * 1000000 END AS blended_cost_per_1m
FROM econ
LEFT JOIN sig
  ON econ.hour_ts = sig.hour_ts
 AND econ.region_norm = sig.region_norm
 AND econ.customer_tier = sig.customer_tier
 AND econ.model_key = sig.model_key
 AND econ.quantization_profile = sig.quantization_profile;

Perf notes
- If we do this at query time for every dashboard request, it can blow up depending on signal table size.
- Preferred: bake signals into UNIT_ECON_HOURLY during aggregation job (left join once per hour), or maintain a materialized view.

----------------------------------------
Reconciliation queries (Finance sanity)
----------------------------------------
1) Total tokens and cost for QTD (by allocation_version)
SELECT
  allocation_version,
  DATE_TRUNC('DAY', hour_ts) AS day_ts,
  SUM(output_tokens) AS output_tokens,
  SUM(allocated_cost_usd) AS allocated_cost_usd,
  (SUM(allocated_cost_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(output_tokens), 0)) * 1000000 AS blended_cost_per_1m
FROM MART.V_UNIT_ECON_HOURLY
WHERE hour_ts >= :qtd_start_ts
  AND hour_ts < :qtd_end_ts
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY day_ts;

2) “Does this reconcile to billing totals?” (placeholder)
- We don’t expect exact match (billing includes margin, credits, etc.), but we do need consistent deltas.
- Once MART.BILLING_DAILY_SUMMARY exists, join here.

----------------------------------------
Warehouse performance notes / gotchas
----------------------------------------
Observed pain points (from Slack thread 1737501201)
- Slow queries when:
  - grouping by model_key across long windows without partition pruning
  - top-N queries with no min token threshold
  - attempting to compute metric from request-level facts

Recommendations
- Partition/clustering:
  - UNIT_ECON_HOURLY: cluster by (allocation_version, DATE_TRUNC('DAY', hour_ts), region_norm, customer_tier)
  - If Snowflake: define clustering key on (hour_ts, allocation_version, region_norm, customer_tier, model_key)
- Materialized views:
  - Daily rollups MV (by model/region/tier) for default UI granularity.
  - Separate MV for “All tiers” and “All regions” to avoid runtime GROUP BY explosion.
- Strict filters:
  - allocation_version required (Finance view); live/preview view can default to latest but still filter.
  - enforce max lookback windows in API (e.g., 180 days) unless using daily MV.
- Cardinality guardrails:
  - quantization_profile allowed-values only (see ENG-8425/ENG-8432). If quant_profile becomes high-card, it will nuke grouping performance.
  - avoid including customer_id/org_id in dashboard-facing views.

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm final dimension keys:
  - Is model_key the join key everywhere, or do we keep model_id + model_version separate and compute model_key in view?
- allocation_version format:
  - propose: "2025Q4-ratecard_v3|alloc_v2|idle=by_tier" (human readable) vs opaque UUID.
- If region_norm is NULL:
  - do we map to "unknown" row (include tokens/cost) or drop? Current preference: include as unknown and surface coverage warning.
- Tier mapping timing:
  - If a customer migrates tiers mid-month, which tier do we attribute? Current preference: derive tier at request_time (snapshot), not current state.

Notes to self (Mei)
- If we keep getting slow queries with multi-select filters, switch API to generate explicit IN lists rather than FLATTEN binds.
- For UI chart smoothing, do not change warehouse aggregation; do a client-side rolling avg.
